decision.title: Laziness, joins and the step limit (packet )

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . Measured with the benchmarks of (tests/bench/run-bench.py, processor seconds, release, fastest of three) and instructions under callgrind; each milestone against its base commit built the same way.

item.p: Why the book's join was slow (docs/book/examples/performance, 2,000 orders, 12 s): //order[@id = $order/@id + 1] is /descendant-or-self::node()/child::order[...] (XPath 4.0, 4.6.7): one FILTER per node of the document over that node's children, inside the for clause's body (it reads $order), so it was never hoisted and only the root's FILTER had 16 items; and its keys are xs:untypedAtomic while the probe is an xs:double, two classes the index of does not compare.

Descendant paths (glossary ; the descendant pass, src/ir_loop_passes.c, a standard pass after verify): E//T[P]... is E/descendant::T[P]... when the step is to the children, T selects XNodes only (node() matches JNodes too), every predicate selects by the item alone (it reads neither the position nor the size, and its value is no number: comparisons, quantified expressions, instance of, castable, natives of xs:boolean or xs:string results, paths, constants without a leading number, through LETs, conditionals and filters), the path after it goes on from each node alone (by-item filters, path steps whose bodies give nodes, document order), and the intermediate values are read once (a slot census of each function's body). One FILTER then runs over every T below E, and its input no longer depends on the loop, so the hoist pass computes it once and the filter index finds the same input each time. E//T[1], [last()], [$n] and E//@a are left as they were. Steps are fewer.

The number view (glossary , src/evaluator_index.c): "=" casts an xs:untypedAtomic against a number to the number's type, or to xs:double when that fails (4.11.2). An index of strings whose keys are all untyped answers a numeric probe value from its number view: the keys cast to xs:decimal (else xs:double) by nearest double, made at the first numeric probe value (a step per key) and stored with the index in the memo. A key's xs:decimal and xs:double casts have one nearest double, so xs:decimal, integer and xs:double probe values find their keys; the predicate decides among the candidates. An xs:float probe value, a key of xs:string (XPTY0004) or one that cannot be cast (FORG0001) leave every item tested, so values and errors are those without the index. NaN is left out. An untyped probe value against an index of numbers is cast the same way, unless a key is an xs:float.

Probes that are no constant first: of the necessary comparisons that split, the filter-index pass indexes one whose probe is no constant before one whose probe is: a where over two for clauses (where $b/@id = $a/@id + 1 and $b/customer = "c3") indexed the constant test and kept the join a scan.

Measured (at c48ba8e, without and with): descendant-join (new benchmark: the book's join over a constructed document) 10.28 to 0.18 (0.17 of it parsing the XMark document every benchmark is given); the book's slow-join.xq over 2,000 orders 12.9 to 0.045; the where over two for clauses 1.79 to 0.03; paths 0.64 to 0.21; xmark-all 1.27 to 1.10; predicate-join 1.79 to 1.54 x 10^9 instructions; xmark-q8, q9, q11 and numeric-join the same instructions. Every benchmark's output is the same byte for byte. QT4 XQ40 and XT40 whole, release, case by case: 0 outcomes differ.

Item demands (glossary ; the demand pass, src/ir_loop_passes.c, after hoist): sxml_ir_expression.item_demand (in the padding after the source span; not in the text form) is the number of leading items the expression's consumer reads, 0 for all. fn:exists, fn:empty and fn:head read one item of their argument; fn:boolean, fn:not, fn:zero-or-one, fn:exactly-one and a conditional's condition two (the effective boolean value's FORG0006 and the cardinality checks see a second item: XPath 4.0, 2.6.4 does not let a processor skip a cardinality check); a FILTER by a constant position k reads k of its input; a predicate whose value is no number and a quantified condition read two. A LET's bound expression gets its variable's demand when every read of the variable is such a read (the largest); a DOCUMENT_ORDER passes its demand to the path's MAP when that MAP's body gives one origin's nodes in document order (a forward step from the focus, a path's document order, filters of them); LET bodies, conditional branches and MAP bodies (plain MAPs, ordered path MAPs) have their parent's. Content LETs () have none. At run time (src/evaluator.c) a MAP or FILTER stops once its builder has that many items (a path's MAP only over one origin: over several its first items are not the first in document order), unless its task delivers (); a forward axis step from an XNode stops after that many nodes of each origin (sxml_step_request.maximum_node_count); the traversals fn:filter, fn:for-each, fn:index-where and fn:take-while of a static call finish once they have made that many (sxml_native_step_request.item_demand). The items after the ones read are not evaluated, nor their errors raised (2.6.4: the outcome is V or an error). The effective boolean value of a node sequence reads a second node it does not need (demand 2 is shared with the cardinality checks); of atomic items it must read on to find whether there is a second (FORG0006), so if ((1 to 1e9)[. = 3]) still reads the range.

Quantified fusion (glossary ; the fusion pass, after filter-index): some/every $x in S satisfies C whose S is a slot read once, by the QUANTIFIED alone, bound in the same evaluation (its LET's body reaches the QUANTIFIED through LETs and conditional branches only, so S is made once either way) to a FILTER that selects by the item alone without a filter index, or to a MAP without flags that reads neither the position nor the size, runs over that FILTER's or MAP's input: the condition becomes LET(p, P, CONDITIONAL(p, LET(x, focus, C), k)) (k false for some, true for every) or LET(t, B, QUANTIFIED(t, x, C)), and the LET of S its body. P stays guarded by the item, C by P (2.6.5). Steps per item are a few more for a fused FILTER (the LET and the conditional) when the quantifier reads the whole input.

One mechanism: a value is read as far as its consumer needs, the demand saying how far, and fusion letting a quantifier read its producer's items one by one; both are IR passes over the one IR, and the evaluator only stops loops that the IR says may stop. holds (explicit stacks; no recursion), and step counts are those of the work done.

The step bound ('s default): measured with a counting build, XMark-All takes 12.3 million steps in 0.83 s of evaluation, recursion 11.6 million in 0.55 s, xmark-q11 5.7 million in 0.4 s, flwor-order 2.7 million in 0.37 s, the quantified loop of 13 million a second: 7 to 21 million steps a second, so 10^9 steps were 50 to 140 s (75 s for some $n in 1 to 1e11 satisfies $n = 0). The default is now 10^8 (SXML_EVALUATOR_DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EVALUATION_STEP_COUNT), 5 to 15 s (that loop stops after 8 s), eight times what XMark-All takes. A step bound, not a clock: it is the same on every machine and in WebAssembly, and a program sets its own in sxml_processor_limits. The QT4, XSLT and XSD drivers set 10^8 and 4 x 10^8 themselves (, ) and are unchanged. The public header's comment on the field names the new default (its text only; the interface is unchanged).

Measured (release, at 6b899d5 without and with; 10^7 items, as without the change 10^8 would take the old bound's minute): exists((1 to 1e7)[. = 999]) 2.26 to 0.004 s; head(filter(1 to 1e7, fn { . = 999 })) 5.72 to 0.004 s; (1 to 1e7)[. = 999][1] 2.12 to 0.000 s; some $x in (1 to 1e7)[. = 999] satisfies true() 2.26 to 0.000 s; empty(...) 2.37 to 0.003 s; with 10^8 or 10^9 items the same times after. boolean((1 to 1e8)[. = 999]) is unchanged (above). Instructions x 10^9: xmark-all 8.524 to 8.608 (+1 %: the passes' compile work), recursion 6.501 to 6.494, flwor-order 4.383 to 4.392, paths 1.750 to 1.753, xslt-key 3.988 to 3.988, match="$var" 2.470 to 2.474. Every benchmark's output the same byte for byte; QT4 XQ40 and XT40 whole, release, case by case: 0 outcomes differ (XQ40 45,964 passed, XT40 12,036). The book's C example makes 195 allocations, 178 before (the passes' scratch arrays while compiling).

Left: two filters in a row ($s[customer = $c][@id = $i]) index the first only, and the second tests the first's candidates (1.4 s for 2,000 x 2,000); loops over other loops (a FILTER or MAP of a MAP) are not fused, so exists((for $x in E return B)[P]) makes the whole MAP; demands do not enter function bodies; the effective boolean value of nodes reads one node more than it needs.
